reuse.why: Builds the new getWorstCaseAmount on the existing getRangeAmount and the shared getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes getScheduledAmount through it, but leaves the preview-transaction amount in shared/schedules.ts on its own getRangeAmount dispatch.

duplication.why: Removes three copies of the missing/number/range dispatch, but the identical dispatch in the preview builder of shared/schedules.ts survives alongside the new helper.

placement.why: The worst-case rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangeAmount and reuses the tolerance from shared/rules, where the matching code takes it.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the amount-resolution sites and their tests.

maintainability.why: One named helper with a clear comment is easy to own, though getScheduledAmount's new optional trailing op (called positionally with a bare false) makes it easy for callers to forget the operator, as several UI callers do.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts preview builder (~line 505) keeps its own `_amount == null ? 0 : number ? value : getRangeAmount` instead of getWorstCaseAmount; SchedulesTable/SchedulesListItem/MobileSchedulesPage/useScheduleEdit call getScheduledAmount without the op.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining preview-builder copy is the pre-existing one left untouched, not a reshaped new copy.

one_place.where: The rule is defined once in getWorstCaseAmount (shared/schedules.ts), but the preview-transaction path in shared/schedules.ts and the getScheduledAmount callers without an op still resolve approximate amounts at their exact value.
